name: Christopher S Ogilvy
identity: Professor of Neurosurgery, Harvard Medical School; Director, Endovascular & Operative Neurovascular Surgery, BIDMC Brain Aneurysm Institute (Boston, MA)
bio: Ogilvy is one of the most senior cerebrovascular neurosurgeons in the United States, with a practice built almost entirely around intracranial aneurysms, AVMs, cavernous malformations, and other neurovascular disease. He co-directs the BIDMC Brain Aneurysm Institute and directs the Brain Aneurysm Foundation, and has authored several hundred manuscripts on open and endovascular vascular surgery. His case mix is cerebrovascular (clipping, coiling, flow diversion, bypass) rather than intra-axial tumor or epilepsy.
training: Geisel School of Medicine at Dartmouth (MD, 1984) · Neurological Surgery residency, Massachusetts General Hospital / Harvard (1985-1991) · cerebrovascular focus · inaugural Robert G. and Jean A. Ojemann Professor of Neurosurgery, HMS; long MGH cerebrovascular career before BIDMC
litt_exposure: No evidence of direct LITT experience. Not in the LITT claims set (in_claims=false, no claims). Entire published and clinical record is cerebrovascular (aneurysm/AVM/flow diversion); no LITT, thermal ablation, or stereotactic ablation authorship or case activity found.
kol_note: Major national KOL in cerebrovascular neurosurgery — director of the Brain Aneurysm Foundation, associate editor of Neurosurgery, hundreds of aneurysm/flow-diversion publications. KOL status is entirely in vascular, not LITT.

name: Ron L Alterman
identity: Professor of Neurosurgery, Harvard Medical School; Chief, Division of Neurosurgery, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (Boston, MA)
bio: Alterman is a functional/stereotactic neurosurgeon who has led the BIDMC neurosurgery division since 2011. His clinical and academic identity is deep brain stimulation for movement disorders — Parkinson's disease, dystonia, and essential tremor — built during faculty years at NYU and as Director of Functional and Restorative Neurosurgery at Mount Sinai (2004-2011). His practice centers on functional/DBS work; the packet shows him as a referring clinician (13 metastasis referrals), not a LITT performer.
training: Albert Einstein College of Medicine (MD, distinction/AOA) · Neurological Surgery residency, Montefiore Medical Center / Albert Einstein (1989-1994) · first Stereotactic & Functional Neurosurgery fellow at NYU (1995) · strong functional/stereotactic pedigree
litt_exposure: No evidence of direct LITT experience. Cohort is 'Referring Clinician' (mets_rn=13), not a LITT-performer cohort, and no litt_perf claims are attributed to him. His stereotactic skill set (DBS, frame/frameless targeting) is technically adjacent to LITT trajectory planning, but no LITT/thermal-ablation authorship or performed cases were found. Practice is DBS/neuromodulation, not ablation.
wheelhouse: Functional/stereotactic neurosurgeon — DBS for movement disorders; division chief
kol_note: Recognized KOL in DBS/movement-disorder surgery (dystonia and PD outcome literature, expert-consensus author, division chief). KOL standing is in functional neuromodulation, not LITT.

candidacy.rationale: Of the three BID targets he is the best LITT fit: as a stereotactic/functional surgeon and division chief he already owns the trajectory-planning and frame/frameless skills LITT requires, and functional programs are natural adopters of LITT for epilepsy. But his practice is firmly DBS/neuromodulation, not ablative tumor/epilepsy surgery, and he appears here only as a referrer. Moderate — credible technical adopter and gatekeeper, but no demonstrated ablation interest; would need a service-line/epilepsy driver to convert.

name: Philipp Taussky
identity: Section Chief of Neurovascular Surgery & Chief Value Officer, Department of Neurosurgery, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center; Co-Director, Brain Aneurysm Institute (Boston, MA)
bio: Taussky is a dual-trained open and endovascular cerebrovascular neurosurgeon focused on aneurysms, AVMs, stroke/thrombectomy, and flow diversion. He co-directs the BIDMC Brain Aneurysm Institute (with Ogilvy) and is surgical co-director of the comprehensive stroke center, having built his reputation on flow-diverter technology and minimally invasive neurovascular techniques. The packet shows him as a referring clinician with a single metastasis referral — no LITT activity.
training: University of Basel, Switzerland (MD) · Neurosurgery residency (incl. Mayo Clinic training) · skull base/cerebrovascular fellowship, University of Utah · endovascular/neurointerventional fellowship, Mayo Clinic · vascular pedigree (prior University of Utah faculty)
